name: HeyDaniel

image.alt: HeyDaniel app interface showing context-aware reminders and task capture
image.caption: HeyDaniel: context-aware reminder assistant

premise: A context-aware reminder assistant: send a task by Telegram, screenshot, or note, and it surfaces the right reminder based on where you are and what your day looks like.
warningSign: It worked perfectly — for me. I poured engineering into the problem without ever checking whether anyone else had it.
causeOfDeath: No market validation. Generalising beyond a single-person use case would have required significant additional engineering, and nothing justified the investment.
survivingInsight: I still use it every day. A tool that only serves you isn't a failure — it just isn't a business. Build the tool first, then find out whether it's a product.
body: A context-aware reminder assistant. You'd send it a task by Telegram, a screenshot, or a note, and it would surface the right one based on where you were and what your day looked like. Walk into a shop, your list appears. Capturing cost nothing, remembering cost nothing.

It worked. For me. Generalizing it for other people would have meant a lot more engineering, and I never got any market validation to justify the work. So I stopped building it as a product. I still use it every day.
lesson: I'll happily pour engineering into a problem before checking whether anyone else has it. Validation first, build second. (Also: a tool that only serves you isn't a failure. It just isn't a business.)
